hypershop-sys: Hey team — our receipts endpoint started returning invalid JSON when we enable structured/json mode earlier today. Parser error from our side: 'Unexpected token N in JSON at position 0'. Happening ~10% of requests. Example request id: req_0a12b3c. Model: redwood/gpt-instruct-4. Any quick workaround? :confused:

sami: Sorry you're hitting this — thanks for filing. Can you paste the raw response body you received (not the parsed object)? Also are you using streaming or non-streaming responses?

hypershop-sys: Non-streaming. Raw body below — we redacted some PII.

```
{"receipt": null, "items": [ {"sku": "TSHIRT-01", "price": 1999} ], "total": 1999}
\u0000
{"corrupt_start": "N\/A"}
```

sami: Ah that looks like an embedded NUL (\u0000) and then another JSON fragment appended — that would break most JSON parsers. Did you see this only for purchase receipts or across other templates?

hypershop-sys: Mostly receipts but saw once on order-summary too. We only switched to structured mode last week.

oliver: tagging eng to investigate. @julian @maria can you take a look? Customer included request id req_0a12b3c and a small sample payload. This is impacting production customers. :rotating_light:

julian: Looking. Initial hunch: tokenizer/response-buffer boundary might inject an extra NUL when a generation finishes and a small follow-up chunk is emitted. Will repro locally with the same model and prompt. Can you attach the prompt template (redacted) and the raw request headers?

hypershop-sys: Sending prompt snippet and curl repro (redacted keys):

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-instruct-4","mode":"structured","schema":"purchase_receipt.v1","input": {"order_id": "12345"}}'
```

sami: Thanks. Immediate workaround options:
- Switch to non-structured/text mode temporarily and parse with your own JSON sanitizer.
- Post-process the raw response with a small sanitizer that strips leading/trailing NULs and concatenated fragments, e.g. run a regex to find first '{' and last '}' and parse that substring.
- If you are able to tolerate minor deviations, use a tolerant parser (json5 or a streaming parser) and fallback to repair.

Example Node snippet we often suggest:

```
const raw = responseBody; // from fetch
const first = raw.indexOf('{');
const last = raw.lastIndexOf('}');
const candidate = raw.slice(first, last+1);
const parsed = JSON.parse(candidate);
```

sami: We can open a P1 for enterprise customers. For customers on Dedicated/Private with SLAs we will treat this as high priority — expected engineering ack within 4 hours and a patch window communicated within 24 hours. For free tier customers we'll still investigate but timeline is longer.

maria: Confirmed a reproduction path. Small follow-up: can you include the full response headers and the exact content-length from the HTTP response so we can see if a chunking boundary is involved. I'll start a triage branch; if we see consistent NUL insertion we'll push a hotfix.

julian: Tech note for support logs: look for bytes 0x00 sequences around end-of-response and any double-serialized payloads. Also check whether customers use streaming + finalizer token sequences — we've seen a mismatch cause an extra fragment emission.

hypershop-sys: Thanks — we'll attach headers and logs now. Can you also confirm whether there's a recommended short-term policy we can communicate to our customers?

oliver: Communicate this: "If you receive a malformed JSON response when using structured mode, please (1) capture the raw body, headers, and request id, (2) switch to non-structured/text mode or apply a lightweight sanitizer as a stopgap, (3) file the raw artifacts in this thread and we'll prioritize based on plan/SLA." Copying support playbook: escalation -> eng triage -> patch -> deploy.

support-bot: Pinned: req_0a12b3c, logs uploaded to case-9843. Escalation level: P1 (pending plan verification).

hypershop-sys: Acknowledged. Appreciate the quick help. We'll hold on rollouts until you confirm a fix.

sami: Thanks everyone. I'll update the customer-facing status page if we confirm a wide-impact regression. For now we've got a repro and engineering is on it. :thumbsup:
